summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and chronic anticoagulation presented with a three-week history of epigastric pain, nausea, and melena. She was found to have acute on chronic gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to NSAID use and a supratherapeutic INR of 11.6 while on warfarin. She received five units of packed red blood cells and six units of fresh frozen plasma, with vitamin K administration to reverse coagulopathy. An EGD revealed esophagitis and gastritis without active bleeding, and a positive H. pylori antibody test was noted. Colonoscopy showed diverticulosis without active bleeding. Her heart failure worsened during admission with pulmonary edema, managed with IV and oral diuretics. She fell near discharge, resulting in wrist and knee pain; imaging showed no fractures, but she was prescribed a walker and wrist splint for safety. Warfarin was held during the bleed and restarted at discharge at a lower dose. She was discharged home with services on optimized heart failure and GI protective medications, with instructions to avoid NSAIDs and monitor for rebleeding.
